stem: A client with diabetes lives far from the clinic and has missed several in-person diabetes self-management education visits because of transportation problems. Which care-planning action is most appropriate?

options.A: Offer telehealth or another appropriate digital DSMES option if it meets the client’s needs and preferences, while maintaining necessary clinical follow-up.
options.B: Discontinue DSMES because education is effective only when delivered face to face.
options.C: Use telehealth as a complete replacement for all in-person medical evaluation regardless of the client’s clinical condition.
options.D: Delay further education until the client can reliably travel to the clinic because remote delivery does not address access barriers.

rationale: A is correct. The 2026 ADA Standards of Care recommend offering DSMES through telehealth and/or digital interventions to meet individual preferences, reduce access barriers, and improve satisfaction. Telehealth can expand access but does not automatically replace every in-person examination or other clinically necessary care. B and D contradict the guideline’s support for remote DSMES. C overstates telehealth by treating it as a universal substitute for all in-person clinical assessment.
educational_objective: Use telehealth or digital DSMES to reduce access barriers when appropriate while preserving individualized in-person assessment and follow-up when clinically needed.
source_organization: American Diabetes Association Professional Practice Committee
source_document_title: Facilitating Positive Health Behaviors and Well-being to Improve Health Outcomes: Standards of Care in Diabetes—2026
source_locator: DSMES Recommendation 5.6 — offer DSMES via telehealth and/or digital interventions to meet individual preferences, reduce access barriers, and improve satisfaction; person-centered DSMES recommendations 5.1–5.5
source_claim_supported: Current ADA standards support telehealth/digital delivery of DSMES to reduce access barriers and meet individual preferences without establishing that remote care universally replaces all in-person clinical evaluation.
blueprint_source_organization: National Council of State Boards of Nursing
blueprint_locator: Safe and Effective Care Environment — Management of Care; coordinate accessible services, referrals, continuity, and technology-supported care based on client needs
blueprint_topic: Management of Care — telehealth access to diabetes self-management education
correction_summary: Rebuilt the source item because the claim that remote glucose sharing necessarily produces more frequent monitoring and timely intervention was broader than the cited evidence. The final item uses the exact ADA 2026 telehealth DSMES recommendation: reduce access barriers and meet client preferences without claiming telehealth replaces all in-person care.
audit_reviewer: OpenAI GPT-5.6 Sol — Rule 1 clinical audit + adversarial second pass

audit_findings.source_audit: Verified against ADA Standards of Care 2026 Recommendation 5.6. The direct supported benefits are meeting preferences, reducing access barriers, and improving satisfaction.
audit_findings.claim_by_claim: A stays within the telehealth DSMES recommendation and preserves individualized clinical follow-up. It does not claim specific visit frequency, glucose outcomes, or universal substitution for in-person care.
audit_findings.choice_A: Correct; it addresses the stated transportation barrier using a guideline-supported delivery option.
audit_findings.choice_B: Incorrect; DSMES may be delivered remotely.
audit_findings.choice_C: Incorrect; telehealth is not a universal replacement for all physical assessment and clinical care.
audit_findings.choice_D: Incorrect; remote DSMES is specifically recommended as a way to reduce access barriers.
audit_findings.ambiguity_second_answer: Only A balances access with individualized clinical needs.
audit_findings.cueing: All options concern delivery modality and continuity rather than unrelated technology claims.
audit_findings.blueprint: Management of Care is appropriate because the nurse is coordinating accessible education and continuity services.
audit_findings.independent_adversarial_second_pass: Rechecked ADA 2026 telehealth recommendation, remote monitoring versus DSMES distinction, access-barrier claim, substitution overreach, category mapping, and second-answer risk. No unresolved conflict remained.
